To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an agent based control scheme to stabilize a large-scale cyber physical system over a communication network with bounded packet loss.

we have developed an agent based distributed model predictive control framework for large-scale cyber- physical systems and analyzed the stability of the closed loop system over a lossy communication network.

we have developed a novel agent based distributed model predictive control (ABDMPC) formulation, which is a combination of the model predictive control (MPC) and the consensus control, for large-scale cyber- physical system (CPS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
stability analysis of a large-scale distributed model predictive control system with lossy communication.
a large-scale cyberphysical system with a large number of agents.
the design of an agent-based distributed model predictive control for a large-scale cyber physical system with lossy network communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed agent based distributed model predictive control scheme is stable for any lossy communication network, provided that the degree of agent communication is sufficiently high.

, for a given level of communication loss, the proposed distributed model predictive control scheme can be made arbitrarily close to a centralized model predictive control scheme by increasing the degree of negotiation among agents.
the proposed agent based control design is stable for any lossy communication network, provided that the degree of negotiation among the agents is sufficiently high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of the agent-based distributed model predictive control over a lossy network can be guaranteed if the control decision is reached within a certain bound.

the proposed distributed control formulation is able to achieve the global optimal performance with a bound in the number of agents that participate in the decision making process and the bound is dependent on the degree of lossy communication in the network.
the proposed distributed model predictive control scheme is stable and the degree of agent consensus is bounded by a function of the network loss rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a lossy network, the control performance can be maintained by reducing the degree of agent communication.
a small degree of agent negotiation is sufficient to guarantee stability in the presence of communication delay and packet loss.
the agent-based MPC control can be designed to be robust to the lossy communication network.
